item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
🍌老板是故意给我画饼不让我promote，从l4到5吗？

楼主目前大厂 L4，过去大半年一直任劳任怨，包括周末也经常在工作。老板的要求基本有求必应，也主动给组里 build 了不少 tools、做 knowledge sharing，CR 数量目前是组内第一。
上个月刚把手上 assign 的一个比较重要的大项目基本 deliver 完了。
大概在距离 Yearly Review 还有两个半月的时候，我跟老板在 1:1 里讨论过 career development。我明确表达了自己希望今年争取 Exceeds Expectations，未来升到 L5 的目标。
老板当时的意思是，等我把当前项目做完之后，就可以开始做下一个项目，而且这个新项目有机会帮助我达到 Exceeds Expectations。
所以我一直以为，我们已经对接下来的发展方向有了共识。
结果这周 1:1 的时候，老板突然告诉我，之前做的项目 scope 和 complexity 不够，达不到 L5 level。他还拿其他 L4 同事作比较，说他们的项目比我的更 solid，觉得我目前的 performance 在组里也不算 top。
除此之外，他还说我缺少组外的 connections，没有持续从其他团队的 stakeholders 那里获得 feedback。他希望我表现到一种程度，就是组外的人都会好奇，为什么我表现这么好，却还没有升 L5。
我不否认自己有需要提高的地方，也愿意接受具体的 constructive feedback。
但最让我难以接受的是，当初老板说完成当前项目后，会有新的项目机会帮助我争取 Exceeds。现在他又告诉我，接下来讨论的那些项目 scope 也不够大，无法让我达到相应的要求。
而且所谓的新项目，目前也只是口头介绍了一些 potential opportunities，并没有真正 assign 给我或者明确 ownership。
上次 1:1 我们为这件事聊了一个多小时，但最后也没聊出什么 actionable plan。老板一直在强调我哪里不够 strong，以及其他同事做得更好的地方。
我问他晋升时间线，他说可能要到明年 8 月。
聊完以后这几天都没什么心情工作。
我知道努力工作、CR 多、周末加班不等于应该拿 Exceeds，也知道升职需要足够的 scope、impact 和 cross-team influence。
但我觉得，如果这些是我今年必须达到的要求，为什么没有更早明确告诉我？既然老板知道我的升职目标，为什么当初说可以安排有助于争取 Exceeds 的项目，现在又说这些项目根本不够？
最让我失落的不是没拿到 Exceeds，而是我一直按照之前讨论的发展方向努力，到了年底才发现，我们对目标和机会的理解似乎完全不一致。
想请教大家：

1. 这种情况算是老板画饼，还是我对他的表述理解有偏差？
2. 如果老板一直强调 performance gap，却没有安排能帮助填补 gap 的实际项目机会，这算正常的管理方式吗？
3. 这种情况下还值得继续 trust 当前老板吗？还是应该降低期待，开始考虑内部转组？
之前确实把工作和老板的反馈看得太重了。现在感觉挺失望的，也想听听大家的客观意见。

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.title: MacroMicro How much has Nvidia actually backstopped? Jensen Huang's resignation
item.description:
MacroMicro
How much has Nvidia actually backstopped? Jensen Huang's resignation continues to weigh on markets ahead of Q3 earnings this week. Investors worry a new CEO could step back from Huang's "AI central bank" approach and trigger deleveraging across the AI ecosystem. How much leverage is Nvidia providing, and who gets hit if its financing turns conservative?

Per our data, $NVDA held roughly $650 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments as of Q2, mostly across three areas:

1️⃣ Purchase commitments (~$300B, 50%): Over 90% is due within 30 months, moving onto the balance sheet over the next two to three years to lock in TSMC and HBM capacity. Because this ties directly to chip shipments and core revenue, a CEO change shouldn't alter it much.

2️⃣ Residual value guarantees and SPVs (~$150B, 20%): Includes a $105 billion lease guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center campus. If Nvidia pulls back, neoclouds take the first hit. With negative cash flow, they rely on Nvidia's guarantees for SPV financing on long-term contracts. Losing that backing would make fundraising much harder.

3️⃣ Strategic investments and circular financing (~$25B, <5%): nvidia already holds at least $100 billion on its balance sheet in equity stakes (openai, anthropic, spacex, coreweave) in exchange for gpu orders. another $25 billion is planned off-balance-sheet, creating circular investment-to-revenue risk.

near term, nvidia has ample cushion. it holds $99.4 billion in cash and short-term investments, plus $320 billion in projected free cash flow over the next four quarters, giving it over $400 billion in liquidity. even after nearly $180 billion in remaining buybacks, it keeps a $220 billion cash buffer. if management turns conservative, new commitments will likely stay within that limit.

with hardware supply still tight, nvidia will likely honor its purchase commitments to recognize revenue. we believe the real risk is a long-term strategy shift:

📌 funding: without new nvidia guarantees, neocloud funding gaps could widen quickly.
📌 supply chain and valuations: slower ai deployment would delay supply chain upgrades and pressure valuations.
tweet

item.title: Daily Dose of Data Science Stanford reinvented text generation. (it’s neither au
item.description:
Daily Dose of Data Science
Stanford reinvented text generation.

(it’s neither autoregressive nor diffusion)

Autoregressive LLMs generate one token at a time. Longer answers require longer chains of sequential predictions.

Diffusion LLMs generate many tokens in parallel, but still need repeated refinement passes. Each pass processes the full sequence, and quality drops quickly when you cut the passes.

Stanford researchers proposed another approach, Next-Concept Modeling (NCM). It generates text from coarse structure to fine detail in roughly a dozen passes.

First, a tokenizer learns to represent text as layers of compressed information. Early layers capture broad structure, while later layers add details the earlier ones missed.

A transformer then learns to generate these layers in order, predicting everything within each layer simultaneously. A decoder converts the completed representation into text.

The advantage is that early layers are tiny. Generation needs fewer passes, and those early passes process much less information.

You can see this in the team’s translation example. Early layers produce rough, repetitive text, which later layers refine into a clean translation.

In the researchers’ tests, NCM generated text 10–31× faster than strong diffusion baselines, with comparable or better benchmark scores. On LM1B and OpenWebText, it also used roughly 4–5× fewer training tokens, including tokenizer training.

That speed can also improve quality. Generating several candidates and selecting one based on agreement outperformed diffusion baselines at the same sampling time budget.

The limits matter. Scaling experiments reach 725M parameters, tasks use separate tokenizers, and the release includes evaluation code and checkpoints without a training pipeline.

Some evaluations also use repetition penalties during final decoding, without additional model calls.

NCM shows that parallel generation can work by building increasingly detailed representations. Whether those gains hold at general-purpose LLM scale remains open.

- GitHub repo: https://t.co/gwR7gJHsNA
- Paper: https://t.co/oE7n7gh3Rt

item.title: 江卓尔_莱比特矿池 更新一下短线走势， 目前空头回补已经结束了， （期货持仓不再下降） 但从66k高点开始， 现货和期货CVD都在主动卖出， 因此盘面还是继续弱
item.description:
江卓尔_莱比特矿池
更新一下短线走势，
目前空头回补已经结束了，
（期货持仓不再下降）
但从66k高点开始，
现货和期货CVD都在主动卖出，
因此盘面还是继续弱势阴跌。

唯一的好消息是资金费率已经接近0了，
说明市场做多意愿很弱，
如果有新资金介入，
可能会上涨，
所以就看晚上美股开盘，
有没有变数了，
没有的话还是继续阴跌+震荡。

【特别注意】
短线技术分析只是把裸赌的五成胜率，
提高到六七成，
而不是九十成。

盈利靠的是 技术分析+仓位管理+止盈止损 缺一不可，
尤其是止盈止损。

哪怕胜率只有50%，
只要你做到每次对时赚2万，
每次错时亏1万，
都能稳定盈利。

刚才说 “目前的反弹到66k（最多到67.5k）就是最高”，
有人问为什么。

因为这一轮反弹，
是空头拥挤、回补导致的反弹，
不是多头买入导致的反弹。

出现了以下特征：
1、最低点出现了资金费率负数，
此处做空的人拥挤，
导致了V型反转。

2、持仓量下降，
空头主动回补平仓。

3、现货CVD基本横着，
说明即使跌成这个样子，
也没人买现货，
大家都预期还没到底。

空头回补导致的反弹，
是一次性的弱势反弹，
空头回补的燃料耗尽，
就涨不上去了，
也就是现在的情况。

不像多头买入导致的反弹，
有可能一直持续下去，
甚至走成反转 ： ） - 江卓尔_莱比特矿池
tweet

item.title: Naval RT @RonDeSantis : The Electoral College reflects the fact that the US is a
item.description:
Naval
RT @RonDeSantis: The Electoral College reflects the fact that the US is a republic. The Founders wanted a constitutional system based on the consent of the governed, but they wanted filtering mechanisms so that the will of the people would be channeled towards the public good. And they wanted the role of the states respected.

The EC also guarantees that in an “extended republic” like the US, a candidate cannot just run up the score in one region of the country.

In our time, the EC serves to produce a clearer and more decisive winner (see, eg, Bill Clinton winning 43% of the popular vote but a strong majority in the EC) and focuses election administration in individual states, which reduces complexity in a close race.

We should be doing more to bolster federalism and the role states play, not further weaken them.

There is no reason to change the Electoral College.

https://t.co/vO38mQNfSM - Save Our States

item.title: Avi Chawla Skills 2.0 is here! (8x fewer tokens and 2x faster) We package repeat
item.description:
Avi Chawla
Skills 2.0 is here!

(8x fewer tokens and 2x faster)

We package repeated workflows as skills all the time, but the agent still re-reads the skill and decides every step on every run, which costs tokens and time.

Devs just open-sourced Swamp, where your coding agent turns a repeated skill into a workflow that it builds once and runs again and again.

You describe the task once, and the agent breaks it into reusable behaviors connected in a workflow.

Every behavior has typed inputs and outputs, and plain code decides which step runs next. Swamp then gives you:

- model calls only on steps that need judgment
- secrets pulled from vaults and redacted from output
- versioned data from every run that you can query later
- a full record of what happened on each run

Here's the repo: https://t.co/GtaNpqAngp

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

Swamp plugs into the coding agent you already use, like:

- Claude Code
- Codex
- Cursor
- OpenCode
- And 5 more agent harnesses

In Swamp, the model is a step in the workflow, not the thing deciding what happens next.

The model steps still reason like any LLM call.

However, in this case, code owns the loop, so the agent doesn't spend tokens rediscovering the same process every time.

Here's an official result, where they turned a code-review skill into a Swamp workflow:

- Skill in Codex: about 4.6M tokens, 23 agents, 12.8 minutes
- Swamp workflow: about 506K tokens, 3 agents, 6.6 minutes

That is ~8x fewer tokens in about half the time, and most of the savings came from replacing the coordinator agent with plain code.

You can keep using skills while you prototype. Once a task starts repeating, ask your agent to turn it into a Swamp workflow.

This helps answer practical questions such as:

- Which steps actually need a model?
- What exactly happened on last week's run?
- Can a cheaper model handle the one step that needs judgment?

Once it's built, you can run the workflow from your agent, the CLI, a schedule, or an API, with every run recorded.

So you are no longer paying a model to figure out the same workflow on every run.

Instead, you spend tokens only on the steps where the model's judgment adds something.

The animation below shows how Swamp differs from Skills, and I worked with the team to put this together.

If you want to understand the coordination layer that Swamp replaces with code, I wrote a full breakdown of how Claude Code splits work across subagents and agent teams.

It covers when a single subagent is enough, when you need a team of agents that coordinate with each other, and what that coordination costs in context and tokens.

Read it below.

https://t.co/lVnuSmNYo7 - Avi Chawla
